The best TikTok creator outreach message is short, specific to their content, clear on the product and commission, and easy to say yes to. Most first messages get ignored, so the follow-up matters as much as the opener. Below are templates you can adapt for DMs, Target Collaboration invites, and follow-ups, plus the rules that decide whether they land.

Outreach is one piece of a simple system, and the operators running it well keep it deliberately plain. One TikTok Shop seller laid out their whole process in a single post: start with "1 to 3 hero products, a strong TikTok-exclusive offer, competitive creator commissions, consistent sample outreach, clear hooks, not rigid scripts" (@jordantwestecom on X). Notice outreach sits next to the offer and the commission, not on its own. A great message for a weak offer still fails. The templates below assume the offer is already worth saying yes to.

The rules first

  • Reference their actual content. One specific line proves you are not mass-blasting.
  • Lead with the offer. Free product plus a clear commission, up front.
  • Keep it short. Three or four sentences. Creators skim.
  • Make the yes easy. One clear next step.
  • Follow up once or twice. Politely. Most replies come after the first nudge.

Template 1: First DM

Hi [name], loved your recent [specific product/video] post, your [niche] content actually sells. We make [product] and think it would fit your audience. Happy to send a free one plus [X]% commission on any sales you drive. Want me to ship it out?

Why it works: specific compliment, clear product, concrete offer, easy yes.

Template 2: Target Collaboration invite note

Hi [name], sending a Target Collaboration invite for [product]. Free sample on us, [X]% commission, and full creative freedom, your style sells better than any script we could write. Grab it here and let us know if you have questions.

Why it works: reinforces creative freedom, which top creators value, and restates the offer.

Template 3: Follow-up after silence

Hey [name], no worries if now is not the time, just wanted to make sure my note did not get buried. Still happy to send [product] over with the [X]% commission whenever you are open to it.

Why it works: low pressure, restates the offer, gives an easy out that often gets a yes.

Template 4: Follow-up after the box arrives

Hi [name], saw [product] was delivered, hope you love it. Whenever you post, tag [handle] and your commission tracks automatically. Two things that tend to land with your audience: [hook idea] and [proof point]. Excited to see your take.

Why it works: nudges the post, makes tracking clear, and hands them a hook without scripting the whole video. Pair this with a real brief.

Where outreach fits

Outreach is step two of recruiting, after you have found and vetted the right creators, and it feeds directly into seeding. Blasting these templates at unvetted creators still fails; sending them to proven category sellers is what gets replies.

The takeaway

Personalize the first line, front-load the offer, keep it short, and follow up. Outreach is a numbers game only after it is a fit game, so aim these at the right creators and the reply rate takes care of itself.

Hate writing outreach? Book a call and we will run it, or find the right creators to send these to.
